description: Mercimek Corbasi is a quintessential Turkish red lentil soup, cherished for its comforting warmth and vibrant flavor. This creamy, hearty soup is a staple in Turkish homes, often served with a squeeze of lemon and a drizzle of chili-infused butter. It's a simple yet incredibly satisfying dish, perfect for any time of year.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Vegetables
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. Dice the onion and carrot finely. Mince the garlic cloves.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and carrot, sautéing until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add Tomato Paste and Lentils
instructions.text: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot and stir to combine with the vegetables and paste.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the chicken or vegetable broth (or water). Season with salt and black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Blend to Creaminess
instructions.text: Carefully use an immersion blender to blend the soup directly in the pot until it is smooth and creamy. If you dont have an immersion blender, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.

instructions.title: Prepare the Chili-Mint Butter Topping
instructions.text: While the soup simmers or after blending, melt the butter in a small pan over medium-low heat. Add the dried mint and red pepper flakes (Pul Biber) and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle each serving generously with the chili-mint butter topping. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing, as the lemon brightens the flavors beautifully.

tips: For an extra smooth soup, you can pass the blended soup through a fine-mesh sieve, though this is optional and not traditionally done.
Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes in the butter topping according to your spice preference. Turkish Pul Biber is mild to medium spicy.
Mercimek Corbasi thickens as it cools. If reheating, you may need to add a little more water or broth to reach your desired consistency.
article:
From the bustling bazaars of Istanbul to the serene villages nestled in Anatolia, one dish consistently graces every Turkish table: Mercimek Corbasi. This vibrant, comforting red lentil soup isn't just a meal; it's an emblem of Turkish hospitality, a daily staple, and a culinary hug in a bowl. Simple yet profoundly flavorful, Mercimek Corbasi captures the essence of home cooking and the rich traditions of Turkish cuisine. Whether you're seeking a nutritious start to your day, a light lunch, or a warming appetizer, this beloved soup delivers on all fronts. Join us as we explore the magic behind this iconic dish, delving into its history, ingredients, preparation, and the tips that will help you master it in your own kitchen.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi?
Mercimek Corbasi translates directly to "lentil soup," but it’s specifically known for its signature use of red lentils. Unlike other lentil soups, this Turkish classic is typically puréed to a creamy, velvety consistency, offering a smooth texture that's incredibly soothing. Its distinctive orange-red hue comes from the lentils themselves, often enhanced by a touch of tomato or red pepper paste and finished with a vibrant, aromatic drizzle of butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes (nane yagı). More than just a soup, Mercimek Corbasi is a cornerstone of Turkish daily life, served with pride in every household, restaurant, and roadside eatery. It’s celebrated for its wholesome goodness, packed with protein and fiber, making it both satisfying and incredibly healthy.

## Ingredients for Turkish Red Lentil Soup
The beauty of Mercimek Corbasi lies in its humble yet powerful ingredients, which, when combined, create a symphony of flavors.
*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. Split red lentils cook quickly and break down easily, contributing to the soup's creamy texture.
*   **Aromatics:** Onions, carrots, and garlic form the aromatic base, providing depth and sweetness. A small potato is often included to add extra body and creaminess without needing dairy.
*   **Liquid:** Water or a mild vegetable/chicken broth serves as the cooking liquid.
*   **Seasoning:** Salt, black pepper, and ground cumin are essential. Red pepper flakes (pul biber) add a gentle warmth, and a touch of dried mint can be incorporated into the soup itself for an added layer of flavor.
*   **Tomato/Pepper Paste (Salça):** A small spoonful often adds color, tang, and umami depth.
*   **Finishing Drizzle (Nane Yagı):** Unsalted butter, dried mint (kuru nane), and more pul biber are melted together to create the iconic topping that elevates the soup's presentation and flavor profile.
Fresh, high-quality ingredients are key to achieving the authentic, comforting taste of this Turkish staple.

## How to Make Mercimek Corbasi: Step-by-Step
Creating a delicious pot of Mercimek Corbasi is surprisingly straightforward, even for novice cooks. Here’s a step-by-step guide:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by thoroughly rinsing 1 cup of red lentils under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and excess starch, which can make the soup cloudy.
2.  **Sauté the Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add 1 chopped onion, 1 chopped carrot, and 1 peeled and chopped small potato (if using). Sauté until the vegetables are softened, about 5-7 minutes.
3.  **Add Flavor Boosters:** Stir in 2 cloves of minced garlic, 1 tablespoon of tomato or red pepper paste (if using), 1 teaspoon of ground cumin, and ½ teaspoon of pul biber (red pepper flakes). Cook for another minute until fragrant.
4.  **Combine and Simmer:** Add the rinsed lentils to the pot, along with 6 cups of water or broth. Season with 1 teaspoon of salt and ½ teaspoon of black pepper. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender.
5.  **Blend to Perfection:** Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy. Alternatively, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot.
6.  **Adjust and Serve:** Taste the soup and adjust seasoning if necessary. While the soup is heating gently, prepare the topping. In a small pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over low heat. Add 1 teaspoon of dried mint and ¼ teaspoon of pul biber. Cook for about 30 seconds until the mint is fragrant and the butter turns a vibrant red. Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls and drizzle generously with the mint-infused butter. Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

## Tips for the Best Turkish Red Lentil Soup
Achieving that perfect, authentic Mercimek Corbasi is all about a few key techniques and attention to detail:
*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This is crucial for a clear, vibrant soup and helps prevent any gassiness. Don't skip this step!
*   **Sauté Vegetables Well:** Allowing the onions, carrots, and potatoes to soften and slightly caramelize before adding liquids develops a deeper, sweeter flavor base for your Mercimek Corbasi.
*   **Don't Skimp on the Blending:** The signature creaminess of Mercimek Corbasi comes from thorough blending. Ensure no chunks remain for that silky-smooth texture.
*   **The Power of the Mint Butter:** The "nane yagı" is not just a garnish; it's an integral part of the flavor profile. Use good quality butter and fresh dried mint for the most aromatic results.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Seasoning can vary, so always taste your soup before serving and adjust salt, pepper, or cumin as needed. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice at the end brightens all the flavors.
*   **Let it Rest:** Like many soups, the flavors of Mercimek Corbasi can deepen and meld further if allowed to rest for 10-15 minutes before serving.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Corbasi
Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways. Traditionally, it's served hot, often as a starter to a larger Turkish meal, but it's substantial enough to be a light main course.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice is non-negotiable for many Turks, adding a bright, tangy counterpoint to the rich soup.
*   **Crusty Bread:** Serve with fresh, crusty Turkish bread (pide), a simit (sesame-crusted bread ring), or any good quality bread for dipping.
*   **Pickles (Turşu):** A small side dish of mixed Turkish pickles offers a delightful crunch and tang that complements the creamy soup.
*   **Chili Flakes:** For those who enjoy more heat, extra pul biber can be sprinkled over the top.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprig of fresh mint or a sprinkle of chopped parsley can add a lovely fresh aroma and color.
Whether for breakfast, lunch, or dinner, a bowl of Mercimek Corbasi is always a welcome and comforting sight.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Mercimek Corbasi recipe is perfect as is, there are several ways to adapt it to suit different tastes and dietary needs:
*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** The standard recipe is easily made vegan by using vegetable broth and substituting olive oil for butter in both the sautéing process and the finishing drizzle.
*   **Spicier Kick:** Increase the amount of pul biber in the soup and/or the finishing butter. You can also add a pinch of cayenne pepper for extra heat.
*   **Richer Flavor:** For a more robust soup, use a high-quality chicken or beef bone broth instead of water.
*   **Added Vegetables:** While not traditional, some cooks like to add finely diced bell peppers or zucchini along with the other aromatics for extra nutrients and flavor.
*   **Smoky Notes:** A tiny pinch of smoked paprika can add a subtle smoky depth, though it departs slightly from the classic profile.
*   **Herbaceous Twist:** Experiment with adding a touch of dried oregano or thyme to the soup along with the cumin for a slightly different aromatic blend. Mercimek Corbasi is forgiving and adaptable, allowing for personal touches while retaining its comforting core.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
**Q: Can I make Mercimek Corbasi ahead of time?**
A: Absolutely! Mercimek Corbasi actually tastes even better the next day as the flavors have more time to meld. Store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. You may need to add a splash of water or broth when reheating if it has thickened too much.

**Q: Can I freeze Mercimek Corbasi?**
A: Yes, it freezes beautifully. Allow the soup to cool completely, then transfer it to freezer-safe containers or bags. It can be frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat gently on the stovetop, adding liquid as needed.

**Q: What kind of lentils should I use?**
A: You must use red lentils (also known as split red lentils) for this recipe. Green or brown lentils will not break down in the same way and will result in a different texture and flavor profile.

**Q: Is Mercimek Corbasi spicy?**
A: Traditionally, Mercimek Corbasi is mildly seasoned, offering warmth rather than intense heat. The spiciness primarily comes from the pul biber (red pepper flakes), which can be adjusted to your preference.

**Q: What makes Turkish red lentil soup so creamy?**
A: The creaminess comes from two main factors: the nature of red lentils, which naturally break down and thicken as they cook, and the crucial step of puréeing the soup until completely smooth with an immersion or regular blender. The potato, if used, also contributes to this luxurious texture.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it’s a taste of Turkish tradition, warmth, and hospitality. Its simple ingredients transform into a bowl of pure comfort, offering nourishment for both body and soul. Easy to prepare, incredibly versatile, and universally loved, this red lentil soup invites you to experience a cherished piece of Turkish culinary heritage. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to fall in love with the comforting embrace of Mercimek Corbasi. Afiyet Olsun! (Bon Appétit!)
